correctness.rationale: A binary order-five de Bruijn rotation class has a unique 00000 window. Its cyclic length-five windows make a Hamiltonian cycle in the five-bit binary overlap graph, and conversely; exhaustive DFS rooted at 00000 covers all and only 2048 such classes, with explicit closing-edge and window checks. An independently implemented Euler-edge traversal in the four-bit graph yields 4096 rooted trails and exactly the same 2048 canonical cycles. The exact shortest-absent-subsequence dynamic program follows by choosing the earliest instance of the candidate first bit and inducting on remaining suffix length; its answer for every one of 32 rotations is independently equal to the standard greedy arch count. Exact integer tallies are 512 at circular index 10 and 1536 at 11, with verified canonical-index and symmetry-orbit refinements. The supplied executable re-enumerates and byte-compares all 2048 certificates; this is exhaustive finite proof, not inference from random tests.

originality.rationale: The verified archival starting point is the 1991 work on distinguishing binary strings by subsequences. Later inspected primary work (Barker et al. 2020; Fleischmann et al. 2021; Schnoebelen and Veron 2023) develops definitions, general bounds and algorithms for circular scattered-subsequence universality, mentioning de Bruijn cycles as motivating objects, but the inspected relevant results do not give the conditional distribution over all 2048 binary order-five cycles. A published unrestricted binary-word distribution and the classical de Bruijn count alone do not imply the 512/1536 split. No matching table emerged from targeted semantic or title/parameter searches. Remaining risk concerns unindexed or inaccessible specialized enumerations, not a known covering theorem.

value.rationale: The intersection of minimal-length contiguous-factor coverage (de Bruijn cycles) with deletion-tolerant scattered-subsequence coverage is natural, motivated by primary papers that explicitly connect these notions. Complete order-five classification is a motivated finite cutoff: the preceding orders have 1,1,2,16 rotation classes, whereas this is the first order with 2048 instances and a nonuniform 1:3 split between attainable circular indices. The result identifies the proportion of optimal scattered-universality cycles, with concrete witnesses and a symmetry refinement, providing a small exact benchmark and a selection criterion for universal-cycle constructions. This significance does not rely on computational correctness or mere novelty alone.
